requirement: Habeas MUST bundle a `habeas-requirements` skill whose description tells agents to use it during design sessions and before changing code, tests, or requirement text in a Habeas project, including when the user asks for a feature, bug fix, or other change without mentioning requirements.
rationale:
structural: The requirement's only clause is "Habeas MUST bundle a `habeas-requirements` skill whose description tells agents to use it during design sessions and before changing code, tests, or requirement text in a Habeas project, including when the user asks for a feature, bug fix, or other change without mentioning requirements." It prescribes the skill's name and its description content. It names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or delegation interface.

The bundled artifact is the supplied root, `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md`. Its frontmatter has `name: habeas-requirements`. Its `description` says to use the skill during design sessions and before changing code, tests, or requirement text in a project that tracks requirements with Habeas. It also says to use it "even when the user only asks for a feature, bug fix, CLI flag, test, dependency bump, or wording tweak and never says 'requirement'". That covers every part of the text.

The skill is bundled under `assets/skills`. `Cargo.toml#table[package.metadata.symposium.skills]/pair[source.path]` points the Symposium skill source at that directory, and that integration is governed by `requirements.integration.symposium`. The "bundle" clause does not prescribe a packaging mechanism. A different packaging route that still shipped this skill with Habeas would meet the text equally well, so the mechanism is discretionary.

The obligations are therefore about the content of the shipped artifact, not about how the implementation is built. The root `SKILL.md` carries the required name and description, so no further {impl} root is needed.

behavioral: The requirement has two testable obligations. First, a bundled `habeas-requirements` skill must exist. Second, its description must tell agents to use it during design sessions and before changing code, tests, or requirement text, including when the user asks for a change without mentioning requirements.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_requirements_skill_is_used_for_design_and_before_any_change]` covers both.

- **Bundled skill:** The test loads the skill through the helpers `description`, `skill_md` and `skill_files`. These read the `SKILL.md` that is compiled into the binary with `include_str!` from `assets/skills/...`. `description` panics if the skill has no `description:` line. I did not read the part of `skill_files` that maps `habeas-requirements`, so I take that mapping as given.
- **Design sessions and before changes:** The test asserts the description contains "Use during design sessions and before changing code, tests, or requirement text in a project that tracks requirements with Habeas".
- **Changes that don't mention requirements:** The test also asserts the description contains "even when the user only asks for a feature, bug fix," and "and never says \"requirement\"".

The assertions are on the description text itself, so a description that dropped any of these clauses would fail. I found no behavioral obligation without a test.
